short: Three landslides, the Good Friday Agreement, and then Iraq.
full:
Tony Blair rebranded his party New Labour, abandoned its constitutional commitment to public ownership and won the largest majority in its history in 1997, followed by two further election victories. His first term gave the Bank of England control of interest rates, created the Scottish Parliament and the Welsh Assembly, incorporated the European Convention on Human Rights into British law, and produced the Good Friday Agreement of April 1998, which ended most of the violence in Northern Ireland.

He committed British forces abroad repeatedly - Iraq, Kosovo, Sierra Leone, Afghanistan, then Iraq again. The 2003 invasion, justified by claims about weapons of mass destruction that proved unfounded, cost him public trust permanently and drew the largest protest march in British history. He raised health and education spending steeply, introduced the minimum wage and university tuition fees, and handed over to Gordon Brown in June 2007 after a decade of increasingly public feuding.
